meta.notes: Cambr live road scores. tier S>=79, A 68-78.9, B 55-67.9. founding = editorially validated; discovered = algorithmic. Unlisted feed - do not share the URL.

roads.name: Buttertubs Pass (Cliff Gate Road)
roads.description: A sharp, dramatic crossing between Wensleydale and Swaledale, all sudden climbs, crests and tight technical sections between high Dales fells. Long regarded across the motoring press as one of the great Yorkshire driving roads.

roads.name: R115 Military Road & Sally Gap
roads.description: Remote and atmospheric, this crossing of the Wicklow Mountains runs arrow-straight across open bog before twisting through the Sally Gap. One of Ireland's truly iconic drives, championed by the Irish Times and featured on Top Gear's lap of Ireland.

roads.name: A39 Exmoor Porlock to Lynton
roads.description: From Porlock Hill's brutal 1-in-4 descent to the cliffs above Lynton, this Exmoor classic strings together steep gradients, tight corners and open moorland runs above the sea. Top Gear has called it as complete a piece of driving as you'll find in England — and few who've driven it disagree.

roads.name: A686 Hartside Pass
roads.description: The corners come thick and fast on this Pennine climb, building through blind, tightening bends to a summit café with views clear to the Lakes. A fixture of best-driving-road features, and an easy one to see why.

roads.name: B4391 Blaenau to Bala
roads.description: The Bala–Ffestiniog run across the wild Migneint moors — the B4391's second, wilder half, singled out by Autocar (Dan Prosser) as a road that “has it all.” Fast, open, beautifully sighted and near-deserted; it earns S-tier on the same sweeping-moorland character as its Bala–Llangynog sister, from which it runs separately.

roads.name: B3306 St Ives to St Just
roads.description: Cornwall's wild west coast in road form: tight, walled and exposed, trading outright speed for Atlantic views that stop you mid-corner. A connoisseur's road rather than a fast one, picked out by Top Gear among the country's finest.

roads.name: R574 Healy Pass
roads.description: A tight, twisting hairpin climb over the Beara Peninsula, switchbacks stacked up the mountainside between Cork and Kerry. Irish road authority Bob Montgomery rates it among the country's great drives.

roads.name: B4391 Bala to Llangynog
roads.description: Open sweeping bends across Welsh moorland give way to a dramatic descent off the Berwyn range — confidence-inspiring, beautifully paced, the kind of road Autocar reaches for when there's something special to drive.

roads.name: Blakey Ridge
roads.description: Riding the spine of the North York Moors, this high open road flows fast and uninterrupted for miles, with sight lines that let you read every bend ahead. Top Gear rates it several miles of carriageway genius.

roads.name: A82 Glencoe
roads.description: Fast and flowing beneath Scotland's most storied peaks, the run through Glencoe pairs serious pace with scenery almost no road on earth can match. As much pilgrimage as drive — and a near-universal pick among the motoring press.

roads.name: A57 Snake Pass
roads.description: One of the best-known trans-Pennine routes, climbing over bleak high moorland between Manchester and Sheffield with long, exposed sweeps, big elevation changes and a reputation for closing at the first hint of snow. A regular across the motoring press, from Hagerty to Evo.

roads.name: A821 Duke's Pass
roads.description: Compact but relentless, this Trossachs climb packs in a density of turns that shames far longer roads, opening the door to Scotland's great driving country. Rush calls it the gateway to Scotland's greatest driving roads.

roads.name: A4069 Black Mountain Pass
roads.description: A fast, sweeping climb over the Brecon Beacons, opening onto wide moorland with long sight lines and flowing, committed corners. Windrush rates it among the best in Wales for drivers who want real engagement — high praise it lives up to.

roads.name: B4501 — Cerrigydrudion Moor
roads.description: Another leg of the "Evo Triangle", threading across open Welsh moorland to the Llyn Brenig reservoir with flowing, well-linked bends and almost no traffic. Part of a road network long held up by Goodwood and others as some of Britain's best testing ground.

roads.name: B4560 Beaufort to Llangynidr
roads.description: A cracking little mountain road climbing onto the Llangynidr moors above Crickhowell, crammed with hairpins, switchbacks and camber changes that make it a natural test route. Picked out by Top Gear in Wales and Classic & Sports Car alike.

roads.name: B6277 Alston to Barnard Castle
roads.description: A wide, fast B-road striking across the empty North Pennines, with well-sighted sweepers and almost no traffic between Alston and Barnard Castle. Singled out by Rush in its North Pennines feature.

roads.name: B6255 Ingleton to Hawes
roads.description: A wide, fast Dales B-road past the Ribblehead viaduct and Three Peaks country, trading tight corners for big open sweeps and huge moorland views. Windrush called it one of the finest moorland spring drives in England, and Rush rates it too.

roads.name: A537 Cat & Fiddle
roads.description: The Macclesfield-to-Buxton run is one of Britain's most famous — and most demanding — moorland roads, a relentless sequence of sweeping bends and shifting cambers across the Peak District tops. A regular on Goodwood's best-of lists and a genuine benchmark drive.

roads.name: B6278 Consett to Middleton in Teesdale
roads.description: A long, fast B-road striking across the high North Pennines, wide and well-surfaced with sweeping moorland miles and big elevation swings. Rush reckons this is where the road truly hits its stride — properly spicy in its best stretches.

roads.name: Elan Valley Road
roads.description: A scenic drive threading past the chain of Victorian dams and reservoirs in the Elan Valley, with flowing lanes and dramatic water-and-mountain scenery throughout. Picked out in Welsh driving features by Windrush and Top Gear.

roads.name: R560 Conor Pass
roads.description: Ireland's highest mountain pass, climbing narrow and exposed over the Dingle Peninsula with sheer drops and vast Atlantic views. Autocar made it the high point — literally and figuratively — of its tour of Ireland's best roads.

roads.name: A708 Moffat to Selkirk via St Mary's Loch
roads.description: A flowing Southern Uplands route past St Mary's Loch and the Grey Mare's Tail waterfall, fast and open at the national limit through empty border country. Sunday Times Driving rates it among the UK's top roads.

roads.name: N71 Moll's Gap
roads.description: A spectacular run through the heart of Kerry, climbing to Moll's Gap on the Ring of Kerry with twisting mountain corners and views over the Killarney lakes. Featured by SCC among the UK and Ireland's best drives.

roads.name: A543 (Evo Triangle leg)
roads.description: One leg of the celebrated "Evo Triangle" across the Denbigh moors — fast, open and sweeping, with the kind of sightlines and rhythm that have made this network of roads a benchmark for testers. A long-standing favourite of Goodwood and the wider motoring press.

roads.name: Torr Road cliff detour
roads.description: A narrow, twisting cliff detour off the Antrim coast, hugging the headland with steep drops to the sea and a relentless run of tight bends. Long talked up by Irish driving writers — and by enthusiasts who call it the greatest road in Northern Ireland.

roads.name: Holme Moss Summit (A6024)
roads.description: A bracing climb to the Holme Moss summit in the Peak District, with open moorland sweeps and a landmark TV mast crowning the top. Picked out by Rush in its Northern Peak District feature.

roads.name: Harthope Moss road (B6277 to St John's Chapel)
roads.description: A short, sharp moorland climb in the North Pennines, rising fast over open fell at the national limit with barely another car in sight. Rush picked it out as a standout in the region.

roads.name: A4086 Llanberis Pass
roads.description: Running beneath the highest peaks in Wales, this Snowdonia pass mixes open sweeps with a raw, mountainous backdrop few drives can rival. A cornerstone of any serious North Wales road trip.

roads.name: Bwlch-y-Groes
roads.description: The second-highest public road in Wales — a steep, narrow climb over remote moorland with gradients that test car and driver alike. Featured by Rush in North Wales, though its single-track narrowness is part of the challenge.

roads.name: R668 The Vee
roads.description: A spectacular hairpin climb over the Knockmealdown Mountains, twisting up to "the Vee" with sweeping views back over the Tipperary plains. Singled out by Bob Montgomery among the country's great drives.

roads.name: R756 Wicklow Gap
roads.description: A high, open crossing of the Wicklow Mountains, climbing past glacial valleys and bog before sweeping down towards Glendalough — fast, scenic and gloriously empty. Singled out by Irish road authority Bob Montgomery among the country's finest.

roads.name: Abergwesyn Pass
roads.description: A wild single-track crossing of the Cambrian Mountains, culminating in the hairpin sequence known as the Devil's Staircase — remote, narrow and genuinely rugged. Widely cited among enthusiasts for some of the most breathtaking, lonely scenery in Wales.

roads.name: A894 Loch Assynt to Kylesku
roads.description: A dramatic North-West Highlands run through the wild Assynt landscape towards the Kylesku bridge, flowing between sea-lochs and isolated peaks. Autocar singled it out as one of Scotland's best.

roads.name: Honister Pass B5289
roads.description: One of the Lake District's most spectacular passes — a steep, dramatic climb past the slate mine at its summit, dropping between Borrowdale and Buttermere through some of the finest mountain scenery in England. Narrow and demanding rather than a flat-out blast, but a genuine bucket-list drive that both Hagerty and Top Gear rate among the Lakes' essential roads.

roads.name: A4067 Brynamman north
roads.description: A fast, open climb up the northern side of the Black Mountain, running parallel to its more famous neighbour with high-speed sweeps and wide moorland views. Singled out by Top Gear in Wales.

roads.name: B4574 Cwmystwyth to Devil's Bridge
roads.description: A twisting mountain road through the old mining country of the Cambrian Mountains, near-continuously turning between Cwmystwyth and Devil's Bridge with barely a straight in sight. Widely praised by enthusiasts as a near-faultless Welsh back road.

roads.name: Bealach na Bà
roads.description: Britain's most Alpine road — a dramatic single-track climb to Applecross with stacked hairpin switchbacks and one of the steepest, highest passes in the country. As celebrated for the spectacle and the sheer challenge as for driving flow, and a fixture on bucket-list road features.

roads.name: Glenariff Road
roads.description: A scenic climb up through Glenariff — the "Queen of the Glens" — past waterfalls and forest before opening onto the high Antrim moor. Singled out by Irish road authority Bob Montgomery in his survey of the country's finest.

roads.name: A939 Lecht Road
roads.description: The Lecht — a dramatic high-altitude crossing through the ski grounds of the eastern Cairngorms, one of the first roads in Britain to close when the snow comes. A long-standing favourite that Top Gear has flagged among Scotland's notable drives.

roads.name: A44 Llangurig to Aberystwyth
roads.description: A grand mid-Wales mountain road climbing west from Llangurig towards the coast, its final third opening into something close to driving perfection — fluid, smooth and beautifully scenic. Picked out by Top Gear in Wales and Windrush.

roads.name: Ballaghbeama Gap
roads.description: A wild, narrow single-track squeeze through a dramatic mountain cleft in the heart of the Kerry highlands — remote, tight and genuinely adventurous. Singled out by Bob Montgomery, though its width makes it as much expedition as drive.

roads.name: A2 Antrim Coast Road
roads.description: One of the great coastal drives — the Antrim Coast Road hugging the shoreline beneath dramatic cliffs along the Causeway Coastal Route, flowing and scenic for mile after mile. Goodwood has featured it among Britain's best.

roads.name: A272 Winchester to Heathfield
roads.description: A celebrated cross-country A-road running 80-odd miles from Winchester to the Sussex Weald, twisting through quintessential southern England and famous for escaping the dual-carriageway fate of so many great roads. Long championed by Goodwood and Classic & Sports Car.

roads.name: Strines Pass (Mortimer Road)
roads.description: A tight, technical moorland road over the Strines and Bradfield moors west of Sheffield, narrow and demanding with a relentless run of corners. Noted by Rush in its Peak District coverage, though its single-track sections ask for commitment.

roads.name: A4061 Rhigos Mountain Road
roads.description: A dramatic Valleys mountain road sweeping up and over the Rhigos, with a famous hairpin descent towards Treherbert and huge views across the South Wales hills. Featured by Rush in its South Wales coverage.

roads.name: B6270 Swaledale
roads.description: A long, characterful run the length of Swaledale, following the river through stone-walled villages with a constant rhythm of bends. Less a household name than a local's favourite — exactly the kind of secret Dales road enthusiasts trade between themselves.

roads.name: Unnamed road NW of Elan Village (3)
N70 Ring of Kerry Caherdaniel
roads.description: A stretch of the world-famous Ring of Kerry around Caherdaniel, climbing above Derrynane with sweeping coastal views — spectacular, if often busy with tour traffic. Featured by SCC.

roads.name: A702 Dalveen Pass
roads.description: A flowing climb through the dramatic Dalveen Pass in the Southern Uplands, sweeping between steep green hills on a fast, open road. Widely cited among enthusiasts as one of southern Scotland's finest stretches.

roads.name: A836 Tongue to Laxford Bridge
roads.description: A remote, empty run across the far north of Scotland on the NC500, threading between moorland, lochs and bare mountains with barely another soul about. Singled out by Top Gear in Scotland.

roads.name: B3135 Cheddar Gorge
roads.description: A drive through one of England's great natural set-pieces — the limestone walls of Cheddar Gorge, tight and theatrical at the bottom before opening onto the Mendip tops. Featured by both Top Gear and SCC.

roads.name: B27 Spelga Pass Mourne Mountains
roads.description: A sweeping run up to the Spelga reservoir in the heart of the Mourne Mountains, with open bends and a dramatic dam-side setting. A quiet gem championed by the driving writers who've found it.

roads.name: B66 Binevenagh Mountain
roads.description: A dramatic climb up the Binevenagh escarpment, opening onto a high plateau with sweeping views over Lough Foyle and the Atlantic. Noted in Bob Montgomery's survey of Ireland's best drives.

roads.name: A87 Glen Shiel Five Sisters
roads.description: A grand Highland sweep through Glen Shiel beneath the Five Sisters of Kintail, fast and flowing on the main road to Skye with mountains crowding in on either side. A perennial favourite in driver polls, and one of the great Scottish scenic runs.

roads.name: A498 Nantgwynant
roads.description: A scenic Snowdonia road running beneath the high peaks past Llyn Gwynant, mixing flowing curves with postcard mountain views. A worthy inclusion in Rush's Snowdonia coverage.

roads.name: Unnamed road NW of South Carne
A684 Hawes to Sedbergh
roads.description: A long, open Dales A-road running west from Hawes towards the Howgills, wide and well-sighted with a steady supply of fast sweepers. Featured by Rush in its Yorkshire Dales roundup.

roads.name: A83 Rest and Be Thankful
roads.description: A famous Highland pass climbing through the Arrochar Alps to its well-named summit, with sweeping views down Glen Croe — though landslides and a long-running diversion have dogged it for years. A scenic landmark more than a driver's road.

roads.name: B3212 Dartmoor cross
roads.description: A classic Dartmoor crossing over open moorland between Moretonhampstead and Princetown, with wide views, free-roaming ponies and a flowing run across the granite spine of the moor. Featured by Windrush among Britain's best drives.

roads.name: R247 Rathmullan to Knockalla
roads.description: A stunning Donegal coast road climbing the Knockalla ridge above Lough Swilly, with sweeping bends and views over some of Ireland's finest beaches. Singled out by Bob Montgomery among the country's great drives.

roads.name: B3357 Tavistock to Two Bridges
roads.description: A high Dartmoor crossing from Tavistock over the open moor to Two Bridges, with long elevation changes and that distinctive bleak, beautiful moorland character. Featured by Top Gear in England.

roads.name: A827/B846 Killin to Tummel Bridge
roads.description: A scenic Perthshire run from Killin along Loch Tay and over the hills to Tummel Bridge, with lochside sweeps and open Highland views. The Loch Tay stretch has ranked highly in drivers' polls of Britain's best roads.

roads.name: A2 Portrush to Ballycastle
roads.description: The north Antrim leg of the Causeway Coastal Route, sweeping between Portrush and Ballycastle past dramatic cliffs, ruined castles and the open North Atlantic. Goodwood has featured this celebrated coast road.

roads.name: Unnamed road SE of Combe Martin
A701 Devil's Beeftub
roads.description: A flowing run north out of Moffat past the dramatic hollow known as the Devil's Beeftub, fast and open through the rolling Southern Uplands. Featured by SCC among the UK's best.

roads.name: R568 Ballaghisheen Pass
roads.description: A quiet mountain pass through the empty heart of the Iveragh Peninsula in Kerry, a lonely alternative to the tourist routes nearby. Picked out by Bob Montgomery and SCC alike.

roads.name: A939 Corgarff to Ballater
roads.description: A wonderful Cairngorms run climbing through Corgarff and over high, snow-prone passes towards Royal Deeside, with big elevation swings and open mountain views. Picked out by Top Gear in Scotland.

roads.name: A361 Burford to Stow
roads.description: A quick, rolling Cotswolds A-road between Burford and Stow-on-the-Wold, fast and well-sighted through classic honey-stone countryside. Singled out by Harry Metcalfe as a favourite local route.

roads.name: B4235 Chepstow to Usk
roads.description: A swooping, empty B-road between Chepstow and Usk, a lovely introduction to Wales with flowing curves and views over rolling farmland. Picked out by Top Gear in Wales.

roads.name: A1107 Coldingham Coast
roads.description: A quiet coastal road along the Berwickshire shore near St Abbs, with rolling bends and glimpses of dramatic cliffs and the North Sea. Widely tipped among enthusiasts as a Borders coastal gem.

roads.name: A4059 Hirwaun to Storey Arms
roads.description: A fast, open climb into the central Brecon Beacons beneath Pen y Fan, with sweeping bends and big mountain views as it rises towards the Storey Arms. Picked out by Top Gear in Wales.

roads.name: A93 Cairnwell Pass
roads.description: The highest public road in Britain, sweeping over the Cairnwell Pass through the Glenshee ski grounds with fast, open bends and a real sense of altitude. More bucket-list Highland spectacle than technical challenge, and a favourite among drivers heading north.

roads.name: A832 Wester Ross
roads.description: A sprawling coastal route through Wester Ross, linking sea-lochs, passes and remote Highland villages across some of Scotland's most spectacular scenery. Picked out by Windrush among Britain's best.

roads.name: A830 Fort William to Mallaig (Road to the Isles)
roads.description: The celebrated "Road to the Isles" running west from Fort William to Mallaig, sweeping past lochs, beaches and viaducts with the islands of Eigg and Rùm on the horizon. A bucket-list scenic drive, beloved of everyone who makes the journey west.

roads.name: R559 Slea Head Drive
roads.description: A spectacular coastal loop around Slea Head on the Dingle Peninsula, narrow and winding past beaches, cliffs and the open Atlantic at Ireland's western edge. Featured by SCC, though it's as much a sightseeing route as a driving one.

roads.name: Unnamed road NE of Hathersage Booths (1)
Unnamed road SE of Thornley with Wheatley
A896 Torridon Kinlochewe to Lochcarron
roads.description: A magnificent Highland road through the Torridon mountains, narrow and dramatic beneath some of Scotland's most striking peaks. Flagged by Top Gear in Scotland — as much for the scenery as the drive.

roads.name: Unnamed road E of Llanddewi Brefi (1)
A683 Kirkby Stephen to Sedbergh
roads.description: A wide, fast A-road sweeping down the Lune valley beneath the Howgill Fells between Kirkby Stephen and Sedbergh, open and well-sighted with a lovely natural rhythm. Singled out by Rush in the Yorkshire Dales.

roads.name: B4520 Brecon to Builth Wells
roads.description: A rollercoaster of a B-road climbing onto the lonely Mynydd Epynt ranges between Brecon and Builth Wells, with a smile-inducing run of crests and curves and almost no traffic. Widely cited by enthusiasts as one of mid-Wales's hidden gems.

roads.name: Fleet Moss B6160
roads.description: The highest road in the Yorkshire Dales, a steep, lonely climb over the moors between Wensleydale and Wharfedale that's a rite of passage for cyclists and drivers alike. Narrow and exposed near the top, it's prized more for the achievement and the views than outright pace.

roads.name: Unnamed road N of Langdon Beck
Unnamed road NE of Rhandirmwyn Bridge (2)
B6357 Saughtree to Jedburgh
roads.description: A quiet, flowing B-road through the empty forests and hills of the Scottish Borders, fast and well-sighted with almost no traffic. Widely tipped among enthusiasts as one of the Borders' best-kept secrets.

roads.name: Hardknott Pass
roads.description: England's steepest road — a brutal single-track scramble over the Lakeland fells with 1-in-3 gradients and hairpins that test nerve as much as skill. Famous as much for its challenge and drama as for the driving itself, it's one of Britain's most notorious passes.

roads.name: Unnamed road N of Llansaintfraed in Elwel
Unnamed road N of Stratford Tony
Wrynose Pass
roads.description: A steep, narrow Lakeland pass often driven back-to-back with neighbouring Hardknott, climbing tight and rough over the fells between the Duddon and Little Langdale valleys. Like its partner, it's famous as much for the challenge and the scenery as for the drive.

roads.name: B3276 Newquay to Padstow
roads.description: An exhilarating coast road weaving around the rugged Atlantic headlands between Newquay and Padstow, tight and rolling with the sea never far from view. More about the scenery and the character than outright speed.

roads.name: Unnamed road N of Carr Shield
A396 Tiverton to Dunster
roads.description: A near-unceasing sequence of corners following the wooded Exe valley up towards Exmoor and the coast at Dunster — consistently engaging without ever needing big speed. Widely cited among driving enthusiasts as one of the West Country's best.

roads.name: R335 Louisburg to Leenaun via Doolough
roads.description: A hauntingly beautiful run through the remote Doolough valley in Connemara, threading between mountains and lough on an empty, atmospheric road. Singled out by Bob Montgomery among Ireland's great drives.

roads.name: R571 Ring of Beara
roads.description: A quieter alternative to Kerry's famous rings, looping around the rugged Beara Peninsula with mountains on one side and the Atlantic on the other. Featured on Top Gear's lap of Ireland.

roads.name: Unnamed road E of Walburn Hall
A861 Sunart / Ardgour
roads.description: A remote, lonely Highland road winding around the Ardgour and Sunart peninsulas, threading between sea-lochs and rugged hills in one of Scotland's least-visited corners. A favourite among enthusiasts who seek out the far west's empty roads.

roads.name: Unnamed road SW of Little Asby
Unnamed road W of Cefn Coch (1)
A712 Galloway Forest
roads.description: A peaceful run on the old Queen's Way through the Galloway Forest Park, flowing between lochs and forest in one of southern Scotland's quietest corners. Picked out by Top Gear in Scotland.

roads.name: R477 Black Head / Burren Coastal
roads.description: A striking coastal road around Black Head on the edge of the Burren in County Clare, running between the bare limestone hills and Galway Bay. Picked out by Bob Montgomery among Ireland's notable drives.

roads.name: R562 Gap of Dunloe
roads.description: A famously narrow, twisting pass through the Gap of Dunloe in Kerry, squeezing between towering rock walls past a chain of mountain loughs. Picked out by Bob Montgomery, though it's a slow, spectacular squeeze better known to walkers and pony-traps than fast cars.

roads.name: A82 Loch Lomond
roads.description: The classic run up the bonnie banks of Loch Lomond, scenic and sweeping along the water's edge on the main road north — though its fame and traffic can blunt the driving. Featured by Hagerty among Britain's notable routes.

roads.name: A890 Strathcarron to Lochcarron
roads.description: A scenic Highland road following Strath Carron down to Lochcarron, winding between hills and water in the remote west. A quiet favourite among enthusiasts touring the north-west.

roads.name: Unnamed road E of Dowlais Top
Glen Etive
roads.description: A spectacular dead-end single-track road threading down a remote Highland glen towards Loch Etive, made famous as a film location and regularly called one of Scotland's most beautiful drives. Pure scenery and atmosphere rather than a driver's road — narrow, slow and unforgettable.

roads.name: Unnamed road S of Thornley Gate
N71 Glengarriff to Mizen
roads.description: A scenic run through West Cork from Glengarriff towards Mizen Head, climbing through the tunnels of the Caha Mountains before reaching Ireland's south-westerly tip. Featured on Top Gear's lap of Ireland.

roads.name: Unnamed road NW of West Woodyates
B6355 Eyemouth to Gifford over Lammermuir
roads.description: A flowing run over the Lammermuir Hills between the Berwickshire coast and Gifford, climbing through open moorland with long sightlines and empty roads. Widely rated among enthusiasts as a Borders highlight.

roads.name: Unnamed road N of Upper Barr
B4437 Burford to Charlbury
roads.description: A quick, well-sighted Cotswolds B-road rolling through wooded countryside between Burford and Charlbury, smooth and flowing at the national limit. Singled out by Harry Metcalfe as a favourite local test route.

roads.name: R108 Ballyboughal to Drogheda
roads.description: A surprisingly enjoyable run through the quiet countryside north of Dublin towards Drogheda, with a steady supply of bends through gentle farmland. Noted in Bob Montgomery's survey of Irish roads.

roads.name: A5 — Cerrigydrudion to Pentrefoelas
roads.description: The fast A5 leg of the "Evo Triangle", a quick, open sweep across the moors that ties the loop together with flowing, high-speed curves. Long celebrated by Goodwood and the motoring press as part of one of Britain's definitive driving circuits.

roads.name: Unnamed road N of King's Thorn
N16 Glencar Valley
roads.description: A scenic run through the Glencar valley beneath the dramatic tabletop mountains of Sligo and Leitrim, past the famous waterfall and lough. Singled out by Bob Montgomery among Ireland's drives.

roads.name: B4371 Much Wenlock to Church Stretton
roads.description: A quietly enjoyable run across the Shropshire Hills between Much Wenlock and Church Stretton, with some genuinely fabulous bends as it drops off the edge towards Rushbury. A local enthusiasts' favourite rather than a household name.

roads.name: Unnamed road S of Okeford Fitzpaine
Unnamed road SE of South Radworthy
Unnamed road NW of Llansaintfraed in Elwel (2)
Unnamed road SE of New Alston
Unnamed road W of Beck Hole
A4069 Carreg Cennen loop
roads.description: A quieter loop through the Black Mountain foothills near the castle at Carreg Cennen, with flowing lanes, big open views and a fraction of the traffic of its famous neighbour. Part of one of Wales's most celebrated driving areas.

roads.name: A4107 Afan Valley
roads.description: A flowing run up the forested Afan valley, running parallel to the famous Bwlch road with a fast, rhythmic sequence of curves through the trees. Noted by Rush in its South Wales coverage.

roads.name: Unnamed road S of Withiel Florey
Unnamed road SW of Mt Vernon
Unnamed road W of Parsley Hay
R700 Thomastown to St Mullins
roads.description: A gentle, scenic run through the Barrow valley in the south-east, following the river between Thomastown and St Mullins through quiet wooded countryside. Noted in Bob Montgomery's survey of Irish roads.

roads.name: Unnamed road NW of A' Ghlac
Unnamed road SE of Cogden Hall
Unnamed road W of Tarrant Rushton
A816 Lochgilphead to Oban
roads.description: A flowing Argyll A-road between Lochgilphead and Oban, sweeping past sea-lochs, standing stones and forest on the road to the islands. A favourite among enthusiasts driving Scotland's west coast.

roads.name: B2141/B2146 South Downs
roads.description: A pair of quiet, well-surfaced B-roads winding through the South Downs around Goodwood, with flowing bends and open downland views. Both Autocar and Top Gear have featured this stretch.

roads.name: Unnamed road N of Halton Lea Gate
Unnamed road NE of Temple Guiting
Unnamed road NW of Elan Village (1)
Unnamed road NW of Roan of Craigoch (1)
A84 Callander to Lochearnhead
roads.description: A scenic Highland-gateway run from Callander towards Lochearnhead, sweeping past lochs and wooded hills on the road north into the Trossachs. A well-liked drive among enthusiasts heading for the Highlands.

roads.name: Unnamed road NE of North Brentor
Unnamed road W of Langton Edge
B3306 St Just to Sennen
roads.description: The wild final stretch of the B3306 beyond St Just, running out to where England gives way to the sea at Sennen Cove — exposed and dramatic on the Atlantic coast. A worthy continuation of its famous neighbour, noted by Top Gear in England.

roads.name: Unnamed road E of Talla Linnfoots
Unnamed road S of Daddry Shield
Unnamed road N of Lower Bowdley
Unnamed road SW of Lauder Barns (1)
Unnamed road E of West Flemington
Unnamed road NW of St Ann's Chapel
Unnamed road NW of Y Bala
B1257 Stokesley to Helmsley
roads.description: A genuinely entertaining run across the North York Moors over the Clay Bank pass, with a long sequence of sharp and sweeping corners and twenty-odd miles of moorland to enjoy them in. A favourite among enthusiasts who rate it some of the best driving in the area.

roads.name: B4598 Usk to Abergavenny
roads.description: A quiet, well-surfaced B-road between Usk and Abergavenny, an easy-flowing alternative to the main road with views towards the Black Mountains. Singled out by Top Gear in Wales.

roads.name: Unnamed road NW of Long Compton
Unnamed road SE of Maulds Meaburn
Unnamed road E of Whiddon Down (2)
Glendun Road
roads.description: A pretty run up through Glendun, one of the nine Glens of Antrim, climbing from the coast over a handsome viaduct onto open moorland. Noted in Bob Montgomery's survey of Ireland's roads.

roads.name: Unnamed road N of West Stonesdale
Unnamed road NE of Stanley Crook
Unnamed road W of Brompton Regis
